subject.title: fix: local gateway connections recover after listener or token drift

question: Should setup-managed local gateways default to bounded automatic WSL restart and removal of a fully proven obsolete OpenClaw native listener after sustained transport failure?
rationale: The implementation provides a kill switch and substantial safety checks, but enabling destructive recovery by default changes the product’s operator-intent and upgrade contract rather than merely repairing a localized bug.

options.title: Approve bounded default-on recovery
options.body: Keep the default enabled for setup-managed records only, after fixing endpoint-ownership preservation and documenting the deliberate restart/remediation contract.

options.title: Make recovery opt-in
options.body: Retain the provenance and recovery implementation but require users to enable automatic repair explicitly before WSL restart or legacy-listener remediation can run.

options.title: Keep detection without remediation
options.body: Report the proven conflict and recovery guidance but do not restart WSL or stop a legacy listener automatically.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded default-on recovery
recommendation.body: Keep the default enabled for setup-managed records only, after fixing endpoint-ownership preservation and documenting the deliberate restart/remediation contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR description and current-head proof explicitly request a maintainer decision on this exact recovery contract, and this contributor owns the proposed implementation context.
